grade.first_issue: The claimed uniform bound on primes occurring in the minimal hitting sets is not proved: saying that a large prime will eventually fail to divide some term does not exclude that prime from a particular minimal hitting set, and the unspecified constant N provides no bound at all.
grade.summary: The submission correctly proves a uniform gap bound and gives a useful hitting-set description of admissible successors. However, the central finiteness claim is unsupported, so the finite-state argument cannot begin. Moreover, even eventual periodicity would not imply pure periodicity by the asserted minimality argument; eliminating the preperiod is another unproved load-bearing step. Thus only limited correct progress is established.
strengths: Correctly observes that the prime divisors of a_1 hit every sequence term.
Correctly derives the uniform bound a_{n+1}-a_n<=M_1.
Gives an essentially correct characterization of admissible integers using minimal prime hitting sets.

errors.description: The assertion that every inclusion-minimal hitting set H has |H|<=|P_1| is false in general; minimal transversals can be larger than another available hitting set.

No uniform finite set of primes containing all primes from all minimal hitting sets is established. The argument involving p>a_k only concerns one term and does not justify the existence of a fixed N or P_bound.

The passage from eventual periodicity to pure periodicity is merely asserted. Forward determinism or greedy minimality does not by itself rule out a preperiod, and no backward or global accepted-set argument is supplied.
The displayed definition L=sum_{i=n+1}^{n+T}g_i has an index shift and telescopes to a_{n+T+1}-a_{n+1}, not a_{n+T}-a_n.
